lead_headline: Subscriptions flat for sixth straight day as July's post-surge momentum evaporates — MTD crawls at +1.0/day, matching year's lowest weekly clip

restaurant.blurb: 1 new lead today: Soda Club (Michelin Bib Gourmand pasta bar from NYC) planning August opening at The Ramble Hotel in RiNo.

liquor.blurb: Application drought hits Day 41. Zero new filings detected today — the licensing freeze that began June 1 now stretches across the entire July 4 holiday week with no sign of thawing. Colorado's liquor licensing system remains in unprecedented suspended animation: 12,325 active licenses tracked, but the application pipeline completely dry for 41 consecutive days. Wednesday mornings historically average 2-3 new bar and restaurant filings as mid-week activity picks up. This morning: silence. The freeze has now outlasted every comparable period in the database. With no applications logged since early June, the backlog theory loses credibility — if this were paperwork delay, we'd see batch releases by now. The alternative explanations grow darker: capital markets locked, developers spooked, or structural damage to Colorado's hospitality investment climate. Each blank day rewrites what "normal" means.

reputation.blurb: 6 mentions yesterday — the mid-week dip arrives right on schedule. Week totals 70 mentions across 19 sources, down 8% from last week's 76 but tracking steadily post-holiday. Facebook dominates with 18 citations, Reddit contributes 14, Denver Post adds 10. Google News RSS captured 69 of 70 discoveries (98% of total, highest capture rate in three weeks). Top stories: Capitol Center auction at $1.5M starting bid, Mike Shanahan's $15.7M mansion sale details, Northglenn embezzlement case. The 6-mention Wednesday represents typical mid-week cooling after Tuesday's 10-mention bounce. The 8% weekly decline reflects holiday compression, not momentum loss — sourcing diversity remains strong (19 outlets) and capture efficiency hit a new high. The pattern suggests baseline stability around 70-75 weekly mentions when holidays aren't suppressing volume.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (1 new, 1 canceled) — the sixth consecutive zero-net day marks July's longest stall yet. MTD drops to +9 (+1.0/day), 90-day net holds at +118. The freeze deepens: after June's closing surge delivered +17 in two days (June 29-30), July added modest early gains (+10 net July 1-3), then went completely dormant. July 4-9: six straight flat days, the longest dead-flat streak since March. The +1.0/day MTD pace now trails YTD baseline (−16% below +1.2/day average) and looks weaker than June's troubled mid-month when −9 weeks preceded the breakout. Strip out the June carryover and July runs at −0.3/day through its first full week. The 7-day window (+6 net) only appears healthy because it captures June 30's +13 spike — remove that outlier and the week runs −7. No single-day gains above +1 since July 3. The momentum that closed June has completely evaporated with no recovery catalyst visible.
